content_voiceover: IDA treatment is a favorite boards topic because the answer isn't just give iron — you must treat the underlying cause first, or you'll miss a GI malignancy while chasing a lab value. First-line therapy is oral iron: ferrous sulfate, gluconate, or fumarate, taken on an empty stomach to maximize absorption, doses spaced six hours apart, roughly 200 milligrams of elemental iron daily, continued for more than six months so you replete stores, not just normalize hemoglobin. Absorption enhancers worth knowing: citric acid, vitamin C, and fructose. Inhibitors, a classic exam distractor: tea polyphenols, phytates in bran, calcium-phosphate complexes, tannins, and soy protein — so counsel patients to separate iron from tea, dairy, or antacids. Parenteral iron is reserved for hypersensitivity or anaphylactoid reactions to oral iron, or when you need to replenish body iron rapidly and oral therapy has failed. Memorize the expected response timeline, since boards love to test it: reticulocytosis peaks at 7 to 10 days, the hemoglobin deficit is halved by 1 month, and hemoglobin normalizes by 6 to 8 weeks. If that timeline isn't met, think through the differential for oral iron failure: continued hemorrhage, poor compliance, concurrent ascorbic acid deficiency, wrong diagnosis altogether, mixed anemia, malabsorption, or hepcidin elevation from inflammation or a TMPRSS6 mutation causing IRIDA.
keypoints: Treat the underlying cause first — don't just replace iron blindly
Oral iron: ferrous salts, empty stomach, ~200mg/day, continue >6 months
Enhance with vitamin C; avoid tea, phytates, calcium at same time
Expected response: retic peak 7-10d, Hb deficit halved at 1mo, normal by 6-8wk
Failure causes: ongoing bleed, poor compliance, wrong diagnosis, IRIDA
